# Week 2: Using the Amos program {.unnumbered}

::: {.week-meta}
Core reading
: @byrne2016, chapter 2, pp. 16–68, worked through with Amos open (about 2 hours, practical). Pages 33–39, 51–52 and 61–62 describe Tables View, which this course does not use; skip them

Data
: [Student Life Survey](../course/dataset.qmd), clean file

App
: Identification and degrees of freedom

Task style
: Worked example: reproduce, then change one thing and predict the result

:::

## By the end of this week you can

- Draw a model in Amos Graphics and link it to a data file.
- Set the Analysis Properties you will use routinely.
- Find χ², degrees of freedom and parameter estimates in the output.

## Warm-up

Answer from memory at the start of the session. It takes two minutes and makes earlier ideas easier to recall later.

1. Why does a regression model have 0 degrees of freedom? (Week 0)
2. Name the two ways to set a latent variable's scale.

<details class="answers">
<summary>Check your answers</summary>

1. It estimates as many parameters as there are variances and covariances, so it reproduces the data exactly.
2. Fix a loading to 1, or fix the factor variance to 1.

</details>

## This week in brief

This week is about the mechanics of Amos: drawing a model, linking it to data, choosing analysis options and finding your way around the output. Byrne's screenshots come from Amos 23; menus in later versions are very similar, and the [Amos output guide](../course/amos-output.qmd) lists where everything is.

## In the session

- Drawing tools, naming variables, and linking the diagram to a data file.
- Analysis Properties: the options you will switch on routinely.
- A tour of the output, using the Amos output guide.

## After the session

Work through the core reading with Amos open, reproducing each step we went through in the session. Download Byrne's data files from the [Routledge page](https://www.routledge.com/9781138797031).

## Your task this week

1. Reproduce the chapter's examples.
2. Draw the two-factor CFA from Week 1 (stress and support items) in Amos and run it on the clean Student Life Survey file.
3. Find χ², df and the standardised loadings. Check Amos's df against your Week 1 count ("Notes for Model").
4. If you left it in Week 0, draw the R6 mediation model now and compare its estimates with your PROCESS results.

## For your SEM log

Write your answers in your log first; then compare.

1. Where in the output do you find the degrees of freedom?
2. Which Analysis Properties options will you switch on by default, and why?

<details class="answers model">
<summary>Compare with model answers (after writing your own)</summary>

1. Notes for Model, under "Computation of degrees of freedom": number of distinct sample moments minus number of distinct parameters to be estimated.
2. Standardised estimates (to interpret loadings and paths), squared multiple correlations (variance explained in each item or outcome) and modification indices (to diagnose misfit). Tests for normality and outliers when screening.

</details>
